title: Hogwarts roll call
rule: Named characters from J.K. Rowling's seven novels; a first name or a surname alone counts.

traps.Gandalf: A wizard from Tolkien's Middle-earth, not from Hogwarts.
traps.Hogwarts: The school itself, not a character.
traps.Quidditch: A sport played at Hogwarts, not a person.

fact: Bartemius Crouch Sr is the father of Barty Crouch Jr, the Death Eater who impersonates Mad-Eye Moody in the fourth book.

title: Springfield census
rule: Named characters from the main cast and recurring figures; unnamed background extras don't count.

traps.Peter Griffin: The lead of Family Guy, a different animated show.
traps.Stewie Griffin: Also Family Guy, not a Springfield resident.
traps.Bob Belcher: From Bob's Burgers, not The Simpsons.

fact: Herb Powell, Homer's long-lost half-brother, loses his car company after letting Homer design a new model for him.

title: Galactic roll call
rule: Named characters who appear in the films; TV-only characters and unnamed generic roles don't qualify.

traps.Stormtrooper: A generic soldier rather than a named character.
traps.Ewok: A species, not a single named character (Wicket is one).
traps.Jedi: A class of warriors, not a character.

fact: The 1997 Special Edition of A New Hope has Greedo fire first, changing the original scene where Han Solo shoots him.

title: Middle-earth census
rule: Named characters from Tolkien's novels and the films; unnamed races and creatures don't count.

traps.Hobbit: A race of people, not one named character.
traps.Elf: A race, not a named character.
traps.Dumbledore: A wizard from Hogwarts, not Middle-earth.
traps.Nazgûl: The Ringwraiths as a group; only the Witch-king is individually named in the main story.

fact: The Elves call Gandalf Mithrandir, which means Grey Pilgrim.

title: Seven Kingdoms
rule: Named people and named animals from the TV series, including those from across the Narrow Sea; unnamed extras don't qualify.

traps.Dothraki: A people, not a single named character.
traps.Iron Throne: A seat of power, not a person.

fact: Hodor's real name is Wylis, which the Season 6 flashback reveals.

title: Mushroom Kingdom
rule: Named characters and enemy types from this series and its spin-offs, such as kart and sports games; unnamed generic enemies don't qualify.

traps.Sonic: Sega's hedgehog and a rival, not a Nintendo character.
traps.Link: From The Legend of Zelda, a different Nintendo series.
traps.Pikachu: A Pokémon, not a Mushroom Kingdom character.
traps.Koopalings: The group name for Bowser's seven kids; name one of them instead, such as Roy or Iggy.

fact: Mario was originally called Jumpman in the 1981 arcade game Donkey Kong.

title: Starfleet roll call
rule: Named characters in the Star Trek series and films; unnamed crew members don't count.

traps.Vulcan: A species, not a single character.
traps.Enterprise: A starship rather than a person.
traps.Klingon: A species, not one named character.

fact: Zefram Cochrane's warp flight in 2063 is the event that draws Vulcans to make first contact with Earth.

title: Hyrule roll call
rule: Named characters from Nintendo's Hyrule adventures, plus spin-offs; unnamed villagers and monsters don't count.

traps.Triforce: A sacred artefact, not a character.
traps.Cucco: A creature type rather than a named character.

fact: Tingle is a grown man who believes he is a fairy, and he first appears in Majora's Mask.

title: Dahl's misfits
rule: Named characters from Dahl's children's books; named creatures and animals count.

traps.Snozzcumber: A vegetable from the book, not a person.
traps.Giant Peach: The title of a book, not a character.

fact: The Oompa-Loompas were first described as African pygmies, a portrayal Dahl later rewrote.

title: Time Lord foes
q: A Doctor Who monster or villain
rule: Named villains and monster species from the TV series; one-off unnamed creatures don't qualify.

traps.The Doctor: The hero of the show, not a villain.
traps.K-9: The Doctor's robot dog companion, not a foe.
traps.TARDIS: The time machine, not a character.

fact: The Weeping Angels only move when no one is looking at them, and they feed on stored-up time energy.

title: Shaken, not stirred
rule: Named villains and their named henchmen from the Eon Productions films; unnamed henchmen don't qualify.

traps.Moneypenny: Bond's ally at MI6, not a villain.
traps.Felix Leiter: Bond's CIA friend, not a villain.
traps.Q: A gadget supplier, not a villain.

fact: Oddjob's bowler hat has a razor-sharp brim that he throws to kill, as seen in Goldfinger.

title: Really useful engines
rule: Named engines and characters from the Sodor stories; unnamed carriages and trucks don't count.

traps.Sodor: The island where the railway runs, not a character.
traps.Tidmouth: A town on Sodor, not an engine.
traps.Brake van: A type of railway carriage, not a named character.

fact: Thomas missed the first Railway Series book, The Three Railway Engines (1945), and debuted in the second, Thomas the Tank Engine, in 1946.
